::: {#exm-add-one-smoothing}

#### The smoothed bigram model

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
bigram = (pair_counts + 1) / (row_totals + n_chars)
p_u_after_q_smoothed = bigram[index["q"], index["u"]].item()
p_unseen_min = bigram[~seen].min().item()
print(p_u_after_q_smoothed, p_unseen_min)
```

With [add-one smoothing](#def-add-one-smoothing),
the [bigram model](#def-bigram-model) gives a `u` after a `q` probability `r sprintf("%.2f", py$p_u_after_q_smoothed)` rather than `r sprintf("%.2f", py$p_u_after_q)`.
There are only `r py$n_q` `q`s to count,
so the `r py$n_chars` added ones are a large part of the row.
The pairs the training text never shows now get probabilities of at least 1 in `r format(round(1 / py$p_unseen_min), big.mark = ",")`.

:::
